title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and Public Standards, outlining its approach to developing clear guidelines and safeguards for artificial intelligence use in public services. It emphasizes the need for transparency, accountability, and public engagement while committing to support innovation within a framework that protects citizens’ rights and promotes trustworthy AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has released a plan to regulate artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep exams fair, secure, and trustworthy while still allowing useful AI tools. The policy, issued after a request from several ministers, will set rules and monitoring procedures to ensure AI does not compromise the validity of qualifications and protects against bias or cheating.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, analyzing both the legal risks and the benefits for creators and developers. It assesses the broader societal impact, offering guidance on balancing intellectual‑property rights with the advancement of AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, affirming that there is no room for complacency in addressing the technology’s societal impact. It outlines steps to strengthen regulation, encourage ethical development, and invest in research to ensure AI benefits all citizens.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will examine how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to help stakeholders understand the committee’s role and the expected outcomes of its review.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines concerns and recommendations regarding AI regulation, policy frameworks, and risk management.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how AI technologies are reshaping the regulation of medical products, focusing on ensuring safety, efficacy, and ethical compliance. It outlines strategies for implementing the AI White Paper principles to guide manufacturers and regulators in integrating AI responsibly into medical product development and oversight.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑enabled defence force among comparable‑sized forces. It focuses on using AI to improve operational readiness, decision‑making and technological advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to take advantage of artificial intelligence opportunities. It also addresses how to manage the potential risks that come with AI implementation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and develop artificial intelligence systems, assessing compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommendations for balancing intellectual property rights with AI innovation.
